solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lad collects sort of amber for scientific study

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the boy holds the colour inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy
tan is a yellowish-brown shade, near to amber

explanation.surface: A boy gathers pieces of amber, perhaps fossilised resin, for a school science project.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of plants is one of the life sciences, so it is a scientific discipline.

clue.text: Gallery's participating in chance experiment

indicators.note: taking part in means sitting within, so the gallery's name goes inside the word for chance

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble
the Tate is the London art gallery; with the 's it gives its possessive form

explanation.surface: An art gallery takes a gamble on an experimental show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries; 'participating in' places its possessive inside the gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run of software by outside users is an experiment to find faults before release.

clue.text: Cook, wearing brown and gold, beginning to indicate style of cuisine

indicators.note: the cook is dressed in brown and gold, so those colours go around the word for cook

parts.note: tan is a light brown
or is gold in heraldry
to do food is an informal way of saying to cook it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here taken from indicate

explanation.surface: A chef in brown and gold livery signals the kind of food being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' makes the cook sit between the two colours; 'and' is a link, and 'gold' is the heraldic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Food baked in a clay oven is a particular Indian method of cooking.

clue.text: Nicole's outside playing, in element

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters, here from the name Nicole

parts.note: a performer who is playing is on, as in on stage

explanation.surface: Nicole is out of doors, playing in the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'. Taking the outside of Nicole gives N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas is a chemical element, number ten on the periodic table.

clue.text: Year 8 heading off into empty bus properly

indicators.note: these letters go into the emptied bus, between its two outer letters
an empty word keeps only its outer letters, here from bus
the first letter, or heading, of the number is taken off

parts.note: the figure 8 is written out as a word

explanation.surface: A pupil in Year 8 boards the empty school bus as it sets off, doing things properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty bus' leaves B and S; 'heading off' takes the E from EIGHT, leaving IGHT. Year 8 is the second year of British secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning according to what is just or correct, so in the proper way.

clue.text: Bird with timorous amateur at sea in France

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly or timid
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator or a ham actor
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A nervous novice sailor out at sea off the French coast spots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a yellow-headed bunting, a small songbird common in European farmland.

clue.text: Driving with no reg, unknown's caught — guilty

indicators.note: the unknown is caught, held inside the rearranged letters
driving letters along shuffles them into a new order

parts.note: n is an algebraic unknown, a variable like x or y

explanation.surface: A motorist caught driving with no registration has no defence: they're guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' shuffles WITHNOREG; the 's means 'is', and 'caught' puts N among those letters to make the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being the party at fault, which matches being culpable.

clue.text: Ghana's inner spirit to continue steadfastly

indicators.note: the inner part of a word is all but its first and last letters, here from Ghana

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a distilled alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Ghana's national resolve keeps it going through hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'. The inside of Ghana is HAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to persist and not give up, which is to keep going doggedly.

clue.text: Maths teacher's period for lessons outdoors?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, one who does sums, an adder of figures
the warm season, when a class might be taken outside in the sunshine

explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is' and joins the two definitions. The first is a playful coinage: someone who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm-weather months suit open-air classes; and a person who adds up could whimsically be named for summing.

clue.text: Daughter brought in particular saw for part of joint

indicators.note: the daughter is brought inside the word for the saw

parts.note: a tenon saw is a particular kind of saw, used to cut joints

explanation.surface: A daughter is brought in to see a particular saw being used on a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes into TENON after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibrous cord binding muscle to bone is a component of the structure around a joint such as the knee.

clue.text: Whitish wild cat mostly eating tongue

indicators.note: the cat swallows the language, so it goes inside the trimmed animal
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a puma is a wild cat of the Americas
a tongue is a language, here Latin

explanation.surface: A pale wild cat, half-starved, eats a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the cat's final letter before 'eating' puts the language inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour named after the precious metal is a pale silvery grey, close to white.

clue.text: Sofa where money maybe stored given to Comic Relief fund ultimately

parts.note: a chest, such as a strongbox or treasure chest, can hold money

indicators.note: comic means funny or crazy, so the letters are mixed up
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of fund is taken

explanation.surface: A sofa donated to a Comic Relief fund, perhaps with cash stashed in its cushions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' rearranges RELIEF into ERFIEL. Comic Relief is a big British charity appeal; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-buttoned leather settee with arms the same height as the back is a classic type of couch.

clue.text: Plague grips ordinary ancient city

indicators.note: the word for plague grips, holding the letter inside it

parts.note: to plague someone is to try them, test their patience
o is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A plague takes hold of an ordinary city in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of the Iliad, besieged by the Greeks, is a famous ancient settlement in Asia Minor.

clue.text: Time of year mum meets retired newsman — about half five

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means be quiet, the same as sh

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed newsman goes round the half
retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an editor runs a newspaper, a newsman

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word five is its last two letters

explanation.surface: Mum meets a retired journalist at about half past five at this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns EDITOR into ROTIDE, which goes 'about' VE, the second half of FIVE. 'meets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The days before Lent, including Pancake Day, are a season of the church calendar.

clue.text: Street artist needing grub so desperately in European city

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

indicators.note: done desperately, in a frantic way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hungry street artist desperately needs food in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges GRUBSO into SBOURG. 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Alsace, seat of the European Parliament, is in north-east France.

clue.text: Nuts stop and stare endlessly at this place, somewhere in the sky

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are jumbled
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of stare goes

parts.note: here means at this place

explanation.surface: Someone crazy stops and stares at a spot up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STARE to STAR; 'Nuts' rearranges STOP and STAR into STRATOSP. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of the atmosphere above the troposphere, it is a region high overhead.

clue.text: Corny jokes which go round at Christmas?

definitions.text: Corny jokes which go round at Christmas?

parts.words: Corny jokes which go round at Christmas?
parts.note: stale old jokes circulate at Christmas, as in crackers, and the round nuts sold hot in the street also come round then

explanation.walkthrough: The grid uses CHESNUT, an old spelling of chestnut. An old chestnut is a joke told too often; roast chestnuts are a Christmas tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale, overused jokes share their name with the round nuts roasted at Yuletide.

clue.text: Excited child writer's meeting back in house promptly

parts.note: to be up is to be excited or roused
a tot is a small child
the writer of the clue saying I am gives I'm

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here from house

explanation.surface: An excited child, meeting a writer, gets back in the house on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link. The setter refers to themselves as the writer, so 'writer's' is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for punctually, arriving exactly when expected, so without delay.

clue.text: When redesigned, lass names funky craft in the market

indicators.note: redesigned means reworked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: funky and hip both mean fashionable and cool

explanation.surface: A girl designer names her stylish new boat at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When redesigned' rearranges LASSNAMES into SALESMANS. 'craft' looks like a boat but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill of selling is an art practised in commerce, so a trade craft.

clue.text: One who's 24 perhaps more fit, covering miles

definitions.note: 24 refers to the entry at 24 across, meaning having spare time

indicators.note: the fitter word covers, or encloses, the abbreviation

parts.note: abler means more able, more fit for a task

explanation.surface: A walker who is fitter covers more miles.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes into ABLER after its first letter. 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strolling slowly is in no rush, the way a person with time to spare might be.

clue.text: Race to boost charity held in pub

indicators.note: the reversed charity is held inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: to boost is to lift up, and in a down clue that means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: aid is charity, help given to those in need

explanation.surface: A sponsored race to raise money for charity is organised in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boost' turns the charity upward into DIA in this down clue; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People of the subcontinent form an ethnic group or nationality, which is a race in the older sense.

clue.text: Given small selection of food, bite muffin into pieces

indicators.note: breaking the words into pieces scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Offered a modest spread, someone bites a muffin into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A light self-service spread of a few dishes is a small assortment of things to eat.

clue.text: Some symbols of withdrawn capital

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the hidden letters read backwards
some of means part of, so the answer sits within the words

explanation.surface: Some symbols have been withdrawn from use, perhaps in a capital letter set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds OLSO inside 'symbols of', and 'withdrawn' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on its fjord is the seat of government of Norway, a national capital.

clue.text: Board game clue uncovered cheat

indicators.note: uncovered means with its outer letters stripped, leaving the middle of clue

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: A clue in a board game is exposed: a player has cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple race game with dice and counters is a classic family board game.

clue.text: Having spare time, it's OK in deli to have a wander

indicators.note: the agreement goes in among the rearranged letters of deli
letters that wander move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: sure, as a reply, means it's OK or fine

explanation.surface: With time on their hands, someone says it's fine to wander round the delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have a wander' rearranges the shop into LEID, and 'in' puts the agreement just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with leisure has free time, so is unhurried and at ease.

clue.text: Corporation, at regular intervals, pulls in with barrows

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, and tum is a belly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one, from pulls in

explanation.surface: A city corporation regularly pulls in with its wheelbarrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' in the sense of a paunch is a British joke word. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient burial mounds are called barrows in Britain, and the Latin plural names the same thing.

clue.text: Frenchman stifles oath seeing rat

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the Frenchman wraps around the oath

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
egad is a mild old oath, an exclamation

explanation.surface: A Frenchman suppresses a curse on spotting a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like part of the scene but is the definition, in its sense of turncoat. 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in the figurative sense is a traitor or deserter who switches sides.

clue.text: Flash American store's wrapping dish

parts.note: a flash is a moment, and mo is short for moment
US is short for United States, so American

indicators.note: the wrapping of a word is its outside, first and last letters, here from store

explanation.surface: A flashy American store's packaging is wrapped round a fancy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link. 'wrapping' leaves S and E from store.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert or savoury preparation is a type of food served as a dish.
